methodology: TTM discretionary bike discounts = $26,633 (1.13% of bike list revenue). Forecast engine re-run with the bike discount rate reduced by 0.56% (half the discretionary share), all else Base.

kpis: Average bike discount %, % of bike sales with discretionary discount, gross margin %, conversion rate

title: Re-price or narrow categories with weak contribution after carrying costs
methodology: TTM contribution by category = gross profit after returns and shrink, less merchant fees, commission, freight, 12% physical carrying cost and a 5.45% capital charge on average inventory; fixed store costs then allocated 50% by revenue / 50% by inventory (space proxy). Retail as a whole is -3.8% fully loaded; flagged (more than 5 pts below that, or GMROI < 1.0): E-bike: Cargo/Family (-29.8% fully loaded, GMROI 0.66), E-bike: Mountain (-20.1% fully loaded, GMROI 0.86), E-bike: Gravel & Road (-11.8% fully loaded, GMROI 1.14). Impact = 30% lower average inventory in flagged categories ($41,334) x (12% + 5.45%).
assumptions: Range reduction removes slow C-class SKUs only, so revenue in flagged categories is retained via substitution; price review not included in the impact.
implementation: Quarterly category review using the category P&L; minimum contribution hurdle of 5% after capital charge for new SKUs.
kpis: Contribution margin % by category, inventory turns by category, GMROI
data_status: SIMULATED - illustrative estimate, not a guaranteed benefit

title: Keep the $350K revolver, avoid new term debt and re-profile the term loan over 48 months
methodology: Peak revolver: Base $197,000, Conservative $237,000 (headroom $113,000). Forecast DSCR (EBITDA / interest + principal) = 1.52x; TTM actual is below 1.0x. Re-profiling the $112,500 balance over 48 months ($2,344/month) lifts forecast DSCR to 2.38x and adds cash, at a small extra interest cost.

implementation: Present the integrated model to the lender; agree a seasonal borrowing base on inventory; review covenants quarterly.
kpis: DSCR, interest coverage, peak revolver vs limit, debt-to-equity
